title: Robust deep learning based protein sequence design using ProteinMPNN
layout_note: Panel A (top, full width): on the left a rendered two-chain cartoon (chain A pink, chain B green) above a sketch of two residues' backbone atoms (N, Ca, C as pink and green triangles joined by dashed distance lines) and a peach 'Input' box; in the middle a large light-blue rounded container titled 'ProteinMPNN' holding two white rounded sub-containers side by side (Backbone Encoder, Sequence Decoder); on the right Probabilities -> an 'Iterative decoding' circle -> Sample -> Sequence -> a peach 'Output' box. Panels B and C below are details: B contrasts fixed left-to-right decoding with ProteinMPNN's decoding order on numbered cell grids, C ties positions across three chains with lines from a cartoon to per-chain grids.
grouping: Nested containers: the light-blue outer panel for the model, white rounded panels for the encoder and the decoder. Input and output are peach rounded boxes with bold 'Input:' / 'Output:' prefixes outside the model. Chain identity is carried by colour: every feature grid is split into a pink part and a green part, matching the two chains of the input cartoon. A small legend in B keys the cell colours (grey decoding order, green fixed amino acids, yellow / blue context not used / used).
shapes_depth: Node and edge features are small grids of square cells (edges as multi-row grids, nodes as single rows), pink cells for chain A and green for chain B; '3x' beside a dashed loop arrow marks repeated layers. Thick black elbow arrows, flat fills, no shadows. Structures (input in A, three-chain example in C) are rendered translucent cartoons; the atom sketch uses small black and blue dots with letter labels.
proposed_highlight: The model is the single large tinted container with its name in large type at the top; input and output sit outside it in a contrasting peach, and the decoding-order idea gets its own panel (B) with numbered cells.
lesson: Carry chain identity through every tensor: colour each chain once in the input cartoon and then split every node and edge feature grid into the same two colours, so multi-chain conditioning reads without labels.
notes: Venue = bioRxiv preprint: the PDF header reads 'this version posted June 4, 2022' (v1; venue_source: pdf); no journal version was checked. The figure is one embedded raster in the PDF, so photo_share is null and the rendered cartoons enter the palette.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

taxonomy.task: protein sequence design from backbone structure

core.what: panel A's left-to-right pipeline: protein backbone input (ribbon render, N-Ca-C triangles with dashed distances) -> one large light-blue 'ProteinMPNN' container holding a Backbone Encoder and a Sequence Decoder sub-panel side by side -> Probabilities -> Iterative decoding circle -> Sequence -> Output

relations.form: the input is drawn as a two-chain ribbon render (pink chain A, green chain B) and two N-Ca-C backbone triangles joined by dashed inter-atom distance lines
inside each sub-panel, update-edges / update-nodes steps are closed by dashed return loops labeled '3x' beside the edge and node tensors
a circle labeled 'Iterative decoding' with a 'Sample' arrow loops Probabilities to Sequence, and the sampled sequence is fed back left into the decoder's Nodes
the encoder's edge and node outputs are routed by long black wires, one over the top and one under the decoder, into the decoder's Edges and Nodes
panel B stacks 'Fixed left to right decoding' above 'ProteinMPNN decoding' as two identical small order/residue tables for chain A, with a four-entry colour key to their right
panel C draws a three-chain ribbon render with red tied positions, and black lines from 'Tied across chains' fan down into the same positions of three side-by-side chain tables (A, B, C)

channels.colour: in panel A cell colour = chain identity (pink chain A, green chain B) carried from the ribbon render into every tensor; in panel B green instead means 'fixed amino acids (context)', with grey/yellow/blue for decoding order and context use; in panel C purple/pink/grey are chains again and red marks tied residues - green carries two meanings across panels
channels.shape: grids of square cells = feature tensors (edges as 2-D grids, nodes as rows), rounded boxes = sub-modules and input/output, a circle = the sampling loop, ribbon renders = protein structures
channels.line: solid black arrows = data flow, dashed arrows = repeat loops (3x) in panel A and pointers to the key in panel B, dashed thin lines = inter-atom distances
channels.frame: the blue rounded container = the whole model, white rounded sub-panels = encoder and decoder; peach rounded boxes = input and output

quality.strengths: tensors are drawn as data whose cells carry the chain colours of the input structure, so the multi-chain setting reads through the network; the input is a real ribbon render and backbone-atom geometry; panels B and C each teach one detail (random decoding order, tied chain positions) with small tables beside the protein
quality.weaknesses: long wires bend round the sub-panels (encoder outputs routed over the top and under the decoder to reach Edges and Nodes); green means chain B in panel A but 'fixed amino acids' in panel B; the encoder and decoder sub-panels are near-identical in size although the random-order decoding is the distinctive part; dashed 3x loops sit cramped against the tensors

insights.structure: Panel A spans the top: input cartoon and backbone-atom sketch on the left, one large light-blue rounded 'ProteinMPNN' container holding two white rounded sub-panels (Backbone Encoder, Sequence Decoder) in the middle, and Probabilities -> Iterative decoding circle -> Sequence -> Output on the right; detail panels B (decoding order) and C (tied chains) share the bottom row.
insights.data: Edge and node features are small grids of square cells split into a pink part and a green part matching chain A/B of the input cartoon, so tensors carry chain identity; the input is a ribbon render plus two N-Ca-C triangles joined by dashed distance lines.
insights.emphasis: The model is the only big tinted container, and the input and output are peach rounded boxes with bold 'Input:'/'Output:' prefixes framing it; the novel random-decoding order is called out by text inside the decoder and contrasted against left-to-right decoding in panel B.
insights.flow: Left to right through encoder to decoder, with 3x dashed loops for repeated node/edge updates inside each sub-panel and a long return line from Sequence back into the decoder's Nodes forming the iterative-decoding loop.
insights.avoid: Several long orthogonal lines (Zeros feed, encoder-to-decoder node line) cross panel borders and run under each other, making the routing between encoder and decoder hard to trace.

arrangement.units: one tinted rounded model container holding two white rounded sub-panels (encoder, decoder); input and output as peach boxes outside; two lettered detail panels below without frames
arrangement.inputs_as: ribbon render of two chains above a backbone-atom distance sketch and a peach input box
arrangement.shared: pink/green chain colouring repeated on every feature grid
